sectionMarriagesTitle: 1. Child Marriage: The Case of Aisha
sectionMarriagesIntro: One of the most disturbing aspects of Muhammad's life is his marriage to Aisha when she was a child. This is documented in the most authentic Islamic sources:
ref01Text: Narrated Aisha: The Prophet engaged me when I was a girl of six (years). We went to Medina and stayed at the home of Bani-al-Harith bin Khazraj. Then I got ill and my hair fell down. Later on my hair grew (again) and my mother, Um Ruman, came to me while I was playing in a swing with some of my girl friends. She called me, and I went to her, not knowing what she wanted to do to me. She caught me by the hand and made me stand at the door of the house. I was breathless then, and when my breathing became all right, she took some water and rubbed my face and head with it. Then she took me into the house. There in the house I saw some Ansari women who said, 'Best wishes and Allah's Blessing and a good luck.' Then she entrusted me to them and they prepared me (for the marriage). Unexpectedly Allah's Apostle came to me in the forenoon and my mother handed me over to him, and at that time I was a girl of nine years of age.
ref02Text: Aisha reported: Allah's Apostle married me when I was six years old, and I was admitted to his house when I was nine years old.
ref03Text: Narrated Urwa: The Prophet wrote the (marriage contract) with Aisha while she was six years old and consummated his marriage with her while she was nine years old and she remained with him for nine years (i.e. till his death).

sectionSexualRelationsIntro: Muhammad had special permission to have unlimited wives while limiting other Muslim men to four. He also took captive women as wives or concubines:
ref04Text: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [and] if the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this is] only for you, excluding the [other] believers.
ref05Text: Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Prophet used to visit all his wives in a round, during the day and night and they were eleven in number. I asked Anas, 'Had the Prophet the strength for it?' Anas replied, 'We used to say that the Prophet was given the strength of thirty (men).'

Zaynab bint Jahsh: Muhammad desired his adopted son Zayd's wife. Zayd divorced her under pressure, then Muhammad married her. Conveniently received Quranic revelation (33:37) making it permissible.
Maria the Copt: Christian slave girl sent as 'gift' from Egypt's Coptic ruler. Muhammad had sexual relations with her while she was his slave. She had no freedom to refuse.

sectionSlaveryTitle: 3. Women's Rights and Status in Islam
sectionSlaveryIntro: Islamic texts establish women as inferior to men in multiple ways:
ref06Text: Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [for maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], strike them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them.
ref07Text: And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses - so that if one of the women errs, then the other can remind her.
ref08Text: The Prophet said, 'Isn't the witness of a woman equal to half of that of a man?' The women said, 'Yes.' He said, 'This is because of the deficiency of a woman's mind.'

sectionModernImpactTitle: 5. Modern Perspective: Is Muhammad Followable Today?
sectionModernImpactIntro: Examining Muhammad's treatment of women through the lens of modern ethics, human rights, and international law:

Murder for Marriage (Safiyya): Muhammad married Safiyya immediately after his forces tortured and killed her husband Kinana to get treasure location, then killed her father and tribe. This is murder, war crime, and psychological torture. Life imprisonment or death penalty in all countries.

Accepting Sex Slaves as Gifts (Maria): Muhammad accepted Maria the Copt, a Christian slave girl, as a gift from Egypt's ruler and used her sexually. This is slavery and sexual slavery - illegal worldwide since 1948 Universal Declaration. 20+ years imprisonment.

Sexual Slavery of War Captives: Taking women as sex slaves after killing their families (Safiyya, Rayhana, Juwayriya, and others from raids). This is now defined as crimes against humanity and war crimes under Rome Statute. Life imprisonment.
Forced Marriages After Massacres: Marrying women whose families he just killed - they had no genuine choice or consent. This is forced marriage under duress, illegal worldwide. 10-20 years per case.
Polygamy Without Consent: Having 11-13 wives simultaneously while other men limited to 4. Polygamy is illegal in virtually all countries. 2-5 years imprisonment.

Genocide Complicity (Banu Qurayza): Ordered beheading of 600-900 Jewish men and boys, then distributed their women as sex slaves. This is genocide and crimes against humanity. Life imprisonment, no parole.

Stealing Adopted Son's Wife (Zaynab): Desired and married Zaynab bint Jahsh, forcing his adopted son Zayd to divorce her. Then received convenient Quranic revelation allowing it (33:37). Psychological abuse and manipulation.
Child Development: Modern psychology and medicine recognize that children are not physically or psychologically ready for marriage or sexual activity. Such acts cause severe trauma.

Consent Impossible: A 9-year-old child cannot give informed consent for sexual activity. War captives whose families were just killed cannot give genuine consent. These are coerced and forced sexual relations.
War Crimes: Taking women as sexual slaves after killing their male relatives is now recognized as a crime against humanity under international law (Rome Statute Article 7).
Women's Equality: The systematic subjugation of women in Islamic law violates every modern human rights convention (UDHR, CEDAW).
Domestic Violence: Permission to beat wives (Quran 4:34) violates domestic violence laws in every developed nation. Mandatory arrest policies apply.
Legal Equality: Making women's testimony worth half contradicts fundamental principles of legal equality and due process.
Marriage Rights: Unilateral divorce rights for men and restricted rights for women violate equal marriage laws in all democratic countries.
Age Gap Predation: A 53-year-old man pursuing and marrying a 6-year-old child represents an extreme power imbalance and predatory exploitation.
Pattern of Abuse: The consistent pattern of taking vulnerable women (children, widows, captives, slaves) shows systematic exploitation of power for sexual gratification.

Role Model Problem: Muslims claim Muhammad is the 'perfect example' for all time (Quran 33:21), but his actions regarding women violate contemporary morals, laws, and human rights in every civilized nation.
